newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: PRESS DIGEST - South Korean newspapers - June 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Korean newspapers - June 27.

text.p: The following is a summary of major stories in leading South Korean newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Seoul. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy.
- The Finance Ministry announced on Thursday that it will list Korea Telecom at home and abroad simultaneously in October or November.
- Kia Group received good news on Thursday when the labour union of its automaking arm agreed to let management set this year's wage increase, a move analysts said would reassure skittish lenders.

- South Korea's endeavors to stop Taiwan from exporting nuclear waste to North Korea got an international boost on Wednesday as the U.N. General Assembly agreed to include a related clause in the closing document of the special session.
- On Wednesday, the 47th anniversary of the outbreak of the 1950-53 Korean War, South Korean President Kim Young-sam said Pyongyang has not changed its policy to overtake the South by military force.
- Heavy damages have been inflicted on farmlands and railroads in southern and central parts of the nation due to heavy rainfalls on Thursday afternoon.
